name: lib/retry
title: Retry
summary: Retry with exponential backoff; jitter draws once per retry from an injected Random so seeded runs agree across builds, and never exceeds maxDelayMs.

ts.name: withRetry
ts.summary: withRetry(fn(attempt), {maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitter, retryIf, onRetry, random, sleep, signal, onEvent}).

ts.name: retryDelay
ts.summary: The sans-IO delay before retry k.

ts.name: defaultRetryIf
ts.summary: Everything but rejections and config errors.

rs.name: retry_delay
rs.summary: The sans-IO delay before retry k.

rs.name: default_retry_if
rs.summary: Everything but rejections and config errors.

config.name: jitter
config.rule: none or half (TS also accepts true/false).

behaviour.rule: Before retry k (k = 1 first): capped = min(baseDelayMs * 2^(k-1), maxDelayMs); half: min(maxDelayMs, capped + random.nextU32() % (floor(capped/2) + 1)); none: capped. Saturates rather than overflows.
One draw per retry, and only when jitter is half.
fn is called at most maxAttempts times, with the 1-based attempt number.
retryIf(error, attempt) is asked first: a non-retryable error is rethrown as is, even on the last attempt.
A retryable error on the last attempt is RetriesExhaustedError {attempts, lastError}; its message carries the last error's code, not its message.
Rejections and config errors are not retried by default.
Aborting the signal (TS) stops the retries; dropping the future (Rust) does the same.
